chain.label: FAA/ICAS guidance lacked separation-plan, risk-assessment, and air boss oversight requirements
chain.trigger: the air show guidance provided by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the International Council of Air Shows Inc. (ICAS) did not adequately address the need to better mitigate the collision risks associated with air boss-directed performances involving multiple, dissimilar aircraft

chain.label: Air boss and event organizer had no prebriefed aircraft separation plan, relying on real-time deconfliction and see-and-avoid
chain.trigger: the air boss's and air show event organizer's lack of an adequate, prebriefed aircraft separation plan for the air show performance, relying instead on the air boss's real-time deconfliction directives and the see-and-avoid strategy for collision avoidance

caused_by.evidence: no specific requirements exist for performing documented risk assessments to mitigate risks for air show performances involving multiple, dissimilar aircraft, and neither the CAF nor the air boss had a documented safety risk assessment process for the accident performance

chain.label: Air boss's lengthy, nonstandard radio directives about show lines confused the fighter pilots
chain.trigger: the air boss issued directives that, due to their length, wording, or variations, confused some performers, and the real-time directive he issued for the fighters to cross in front of the bombers ... had not been discussed during the morning briefing

caused_by.evidence: the decision on how they're going to fly and how they're going to operate within the airspace once it starts is ... decided by the air boss while those aircraft are flying

chain.label: Fighter formation aligned with the 1,000-ft show line instead of the assigned 500-ft line, onto the bombers' line
chain.trigger: the flight path for the fighter lead and position 2 fighter airplanes passed the bomber group airplanes off the bombers' left side then crossed in front of the Boeing B-17G, as directed, but subsequently aligned with the 1,000-ft show line (instead of continuing farther across to the assigned 500-ft show line)

caused_by.evidence: he mistakenly believed that the air boss had directed the fighters to the 1,000-ft show line ... he did not fully understand the string of instructions the air boss provided, and he asked him to clarify

chain.label: P-63F's descending left turn toward the show line converged with the B-17G's flight path
chain.trigger: the Bell P-63F was not yet past the lead bomber when the Bell P-63F began to move toward the assigned 500-ft show line, on a converging path with the Boeing B-17G

caused_by.evidence: the directive he issued for the fighter formation to cross laterally in front of the bomber group relied entirely on his real-time, predictive assessment that the fighter formation would arrive at the show line first
The Bell P-63F's flight path closely followed the fighter in position 2 until about 1321:47, when its flight path no longer curved toward the 1,000-ft show line but became somewhat straighter

chain.label: Neither pilot visually acquired the other airplane in time to avoid it
chain.trigger: the ability of the Bell P-63F and the Boeing B-17G pilots to see and avoid each other was limited due to flight path geometry, out-the-window view obscuration by aircraft structures, the limitations of human performance ... and the attention demands associated with maintaining flight along the assigned show lines

caused_by.evidence: the circumstances of this accident underscore the inherent limitations of the see-and-avoid concept for collision avoidance

From 1321:44 to 1321:52, the view of the model Bell P-63 was obscured by the structure between the model Boeing B-17's forward and aft left side windows ... the model Boeing B-17 was visible from the model Bell P-63's flight deck ... but it was likely blocked from view from 1321:50 up to the collision

chain.label: P-63F struck the B-17G's left wing near the trailing edge
chain.trigger: the Bell P-63F was in a descending, left-banked turn when it struck the left side of the Boeing B-17G near the trailing edge of the left wing

caused_by.evidence: the flight paths of the Boeing B-17G and the Bell P-63F converged as each pilot maneuvered toward their respective assigned show lines
the opportunities for the pilots of the Bell P-63F and the Boeing B-17G to see and avoid each other were limited

chain.label: Both airplanes broke apart in flight with fire in the B-17G wing center section
chain.trigger: then both airplanes broke apart in flight. A fire erupted in the wing center section of the Boeing B-17G as it descended

caused_by.evidence: The video showed that the Bell P-63F airplane struck the Boeing B-17G near the trailing edge of the left wing, then both airplanes broke apart in flight

chain.label: Both airplanes impacted terrain south of the approach end of runway 31
chain.trigger: the airplane exploded upon ground impact. The Bell P-63F descended and collided with terrain

caused_by.evidence: Both wreckages came to rest in a grassy area on the airport property, south of the approach end of runway 31

chain.label: Six occupants fatally injured; both airplanes destroyed
chain.trigger: The pilot, copilot, flight engineer, and two scanners on board the Boeing B-17G and the pilot of the Bell P-63F were fatally injured, and both airplanes were destroyed

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for each person was blunt force injuries
the airplane exploded upon ground impact
